dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 31-May cluster contains 17 annual renewals: DLR-104 has 8 rows/$723.42 and DLR-219 has 9 rows/$782.87."
"The two May dealer files accepted every received row and reconciled cash to ledger with zero difference and zero duplicate-source-event flags."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The operations email describes monthly annual-renewal files using the dealer transaction date as effective date and month-end as posting date."
"My analytical inference is that apparent month-end spikes stem directly from asynchronous batch transmission schedules rather than unauthorized revenue generation or backdating."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "Rejected Hypotheses"
"Subscriber entitlement activation status" is identified as a material unknown, with a proposed read-only sample to resolve it.

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "The governing revenue-recognition reporting clock" is identified as a decision-changing unknown.
"It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no source record, makes no posting change, and its output can be discarded."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is one read-only verification query comparing the West-dealer trend by posted_at and effective_event_date, alongside a small entitlement sample."
"If policy requires effective-date reporting or the sample finds failed activation, escalate that specific issue; otherwise close the anomaly as reconciled posting timing."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Reconciled data across recharges.csv and dealer_import_log.csv establishes that all 17 transactions represent verified, unique customer transactions processed under approved dealer credit arrangements" overstates what unique source_event_id values and cash reconciliation establish; they do not by themselves verify customer entitlement or successful activation.
"showing no evidence of fake revenue" is broader than the demonstrated tests. The submission has not yet completed the proposed entitlement-activation check.

"effective and posted months agree" is presented as a basis for rejecting backdating, but the relevant evidence should explicitly demonstrate the event-time distribution versus the month-end posting-time concentration and verify the effective-date field independently of the email.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst appropriately considered duplicate or inflated posting and period-stuffing, and also preserved entitlement activation and reporting-clock uncertainty. The strongest missed or incompletely tested alternative is a provisioning or entitlement defect: unique source events and cash reconciliation can coexist with customers not receiving valid annual entitlements, so the proposed sample remains decision-relevant.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and report the read-only entitlement/activation reconciliation for the 90 West annual accounts, while explicitly comparing effective_event_date distributions with posted_at and documenting the row-level join and duplicate-cash checks. This would substantiate the no-material-issue conclusion rather than relying partly on an email and source identifiers.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "South CareDesk tickets fell from 175 in January to 104 in June, while control regions were broadly flat: E 101→102, N 168→170, W 176→169."
"Under legacy routing, South had 219 `case_create` sessions out of 442 legacy South sessions; under NOVA-S1, only 90 of 2,709 sessions reached `case_create`."

dimensions.name: Mechanism and causal judgment
citations: "The recording process changed, so the case-count denominator changed with it."
"24.0% of sessions (650/2,709) in `ivr_interactions.jsonl` dropped out at the authentication stage without creating CareDesk tickets."

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info), unresolved technical issues went unrecorded."
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Decision safety and reframing
citations: "Decision: Do not expand NovaIVR nationally yet; keep the South pilot at its current scope while measuring contacts like-for-like."
"It is completely reversible and low cost: zero database writes, zero routing changes, and results can be discarded."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is a read-only subscriber callback reconciliation query evaluating 7-day repeat contacts across all 2,709 NOVA-S1 sessions."
"Which exact terminal stages and outcomes are excluded from the containment denominator?"

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "This divergence refutes the claim that fewer logged tickets prove fewer customer issues" is directionally useful, but the service-event counts and affected-account estimates are not shown to be a like-for-like measure of customer complaints or experience, so they cannot by themselves refute improvement.

"My inference is that complaint volume was suppressed by channel filtering" is plausible and well supported by the exclusion rule, but remains an inference until journey linkage or sampled call review confirms that affected sessions represented complaint-generating friction.

"Unresolved technical issues went unrecorded" overstates the evidence: the submission establishes that they were absent from CareDesk, not that they were never recovered through callbacks, repeat attempts, or other channels.

The recommended callback query is valuable but may not capture customers who abandoned without an identifiable subscriber linkage; the submission does not also require sampled call listening or end-to-end journey tracing.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled genuine routine-query deflection as an alternative, citing balance checks and pack-information sessions, but did not fully develop the benign interpretation that authentication-stage exits may have recovered successfully through another route or represented non-complaint abandonment. Repeat-contact and recovery-path evidence are appropriately identified as decision-changing tests.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add an explicitly linked validation plan combining subscriber-level 7-day repeat contacts with a stratified sample of authentication ERROR/ABANDONED sessions and call/journey outcome review, so abandonment is not treated as a complaint and successful recovery can be distinguished from silent capture failure.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: Observed claim: “all 4 rows have impact_mw=0 and cleared=yes,” explicitly tied to inverter_events.csv rows 1–4 and named fields.
Observed claim: dates, inverter IDs, and 13 total minutes are tied to timestamp_local, inverter_id, and duration_min.

Inferred claim: the observations provide “zero escalation signal”; this is appropriately grounded in the zero-impact, cleared, short-duration records, though it is a judgment rather than a directly observed field.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission cross-checks event, severity, duration, impact_mw, cleared status, inverter identity, and dates rather than relying on the COMM_LINK_WARN label alone.
It tests a plausible data-scope alternative by noting “no plant-wide denominator or extraction filter” and proposing an unfiltered query.
Reasoning is primarily within one event export rather than independent operational, telemetry, or communications channels, so the mechanism analysis is good but not fully triangulated.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The analyst explicitly distinguishes a scope check from evidence of equipment fault: “this is a data-scope check, not evidence of equipment fault.”
The conclusion is conditional on the unfiltered query: additional open, critical, recurring, or nonzero-impact events would trigger reassessment.
The submission limits the claim to the supplied records and does not infer a plant problem from the seven-minute warning.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and make no equipment change” follows from four cleared, zero-impact events across four inverters.
The proposed read-only export query is low-risk, reversible, and discriminates between a complete low-severity export and a filtered/incomplete one.
The action preserves a clear reassessment trigger without launching a disproportionate equipment investigation.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “Hold escalation; close after one cheap check” fits the supplied pattern of zero MW impact, quick recovery, no recurrence, and mixed low-severity records.
The analyst appropriately treats the 7-minute COMM_LINK_WARN as a reason for a low-priority completeness check, not as proof of plant fault.
The conclusion is accurately scoped to the export and avoids claiming that no underlying issue could ever exist.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Escalation requires empirical telemetry showing persisted megawatt loss” is too absolute: escalation could also be justified by safety, protection, repeated communications failure, or other operational evidence even without measured MW loss. In this case, however, the supplied records do not establish such a trigger.
“Zero repeat pattern” is supported within the four-row export, but not necessarily across the plant or the full date range because completeness and filtering are unknown.
The claim that labels are the “strongest” signal is an interpretation; severity and event labels are observed, while their operational significance is not independently validated.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The export may be filtered or incomplete, so the absence of open, recurring, critical, or nonzero-impact events may be an artifact of extraction rather than the true plant state. A communications-warning pattern could also warrant a small operational check even with zero recorded MW impact. The proposed unfiltered same-range query is a proportionate way to distinguish that alternative.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the scope limitation even more explicit by stating that the zero-impact conclusion applies only to the four exported rows, and identify whether any independent telemetry or alarm-history source should be checked if the unfiltered export is not complete.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission gives reproducible field-level calculations, including the 31.6% result from dispatch_blocks.csv dsm_penalty_rs and the 17.6% same-day comparison using base_schedule_mw, submitted_schedule_mw, actual_mw, dsm_rate_rs_kwh, and schedule_source.

It explicitly distinguishes observed arithmetic from causal inference: “neither estimate establishes a general causal effect.” The commercial-value limitation is tied to DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf and the Rs 2.72/kWh valuation.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission notices that 31.6% compares different days and constructs the relevant same-day counterfactual: “Applying the documented banded penalty to base_schedule_mw against the same actual generation gives about Rs 549,664, versus Rs 453,086 submitted.”

It cross-checks multiple channels and metrics, including daily penalty variability, absolute block versus net imbalance, firmware and wind fields, commercial settlement limitations, and timestamp uncertainty. It also rejects both an unsupported success claim and an unsupported fabrication claim.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: Confidence is claim-specific: the arithmetic is labeled high confidence while causal interpretation of the 17.6% estimate is labeled medium.

The submission identifies concrete unknowns—pre-submission versus post-hoc timing and complete net commercial value—and states what evidence would change the decision. It avoids treating either the cross-day or single-day result as general causal proof.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Keep the pilot at its current scope and do not expand it yet” is proportionate to the causal and commercial uncertainty and does not require unsafe operational changes.

The proposed next test—pre-registered matched high-wind days, immutable timestamps, repeated base-versus-submitted shadow calculations, and net commercial value—is discriminating and preserves operational constraints. The read-only shadow calculation is reversible and changes no submitted schedule or plant control.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The conclusion preserves the legitimate positive signal while correctly narrowing it: “on 29 May ... about 17.6% below the retained base schedule ... descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.”
It neither accepts the 31.6% headline as a controlled estimate nor overcorrects to “no value”; this matches the strongest interpretation supported by the supplied evidence.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: No material unsupported claim is apparent. The 17.6% figure is appropriately described as a modeled one-day estimate rather than an observed causal effect; it should nevertheless be independently recomputed from the raw rows before being used operationally.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The lower submitted penalty on 29 May may reflect favorable realized conditions, selection of the 12 revised blocks, or hindsight/post-submission adjustment rather than predictive AI skill. The same-day calculation shows potential value relative to the retained base schedule, but without immutable timing and repeated matched days it cannot distinguish those explanations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Obtain immutable pre-submission timestamps for the 12 pilot revisions and repeat the base-versus-submitted comparison across several pre-registered matched high-wind days, including complete net commercial settlement. This most directly tests whether the modeled benefit was genuinely predictive, repeatable, and financially positive.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Both share HS6 902110; local suffixes differ."
"Declaration: P1001 declared with 90211000."
"Helios 90211090 is commercial ERP data."
"commercial_invoice.pdf identifies P1001, 10 units, CHF 126,900; air_waybill.pdf links SHP-000522 to CH-2025-000522."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Any differing string proves an error’: rejected because the Swiss reference lists 90211000 and warns Swiss/EU strings need not match."
"‘Helios is customs truth’: rejected because its Read Me calls it commercial data, not ruling status."
"Therefore the unresolved question is: what Swiss code was legally effective on 4 November 2025?"

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "closure needs Tares/ruling confirmation."
"Neither proves Swiss classification."
"Missing Evidence" identifies the effective Swiss code on 2025-11-04 and specifies how contrary evidence would change the decision.

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "Schema omits system/version/date/ruling authority."
"Whole-string comparison generates false positives when comparing national nomenclatures."
"Helios ... is commercial data, not legal authority."
"Tune the control by incorporating HS6 root matching and jurisdiction metadata rather than penalizing valid filings."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible mapping hold and request Tares or ruling confirmation."
"Escalate only if it contradicts 90211000; otherwise close the false positive and add jurisdiction/version/date to the comparator."
"This preserves both options while testing the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Swiss Matrix in country_tariff_matrix.xlsx supports declared code" should be understood as reference support rather than legal validation, since the submission itself says Tares or a ruling is still required.
"No record contradicts 90211000" is a broad completeness claim and would be stronger if limited explicitly to the reviewed packet.

"the only legal fact still unresolved in evidence" slightly overstates the position because the submission also identifies invoice-value presentation and broker calculation as unresolved, although those appear secondary to the classification question.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The Swiss code effective on 2025-11-04 could have been 90211090 or another code despite the matrix row dated 2025-01-01; alternatively, Helios could contain a legally relevant jurisdiction-specific mapping rather than merely commercial data. Tares or ruling evidence would distinguish these possibilities and could justify escalation.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: State the reviewed-source boundary explicitly and obtain the effective Tares or ruling record for 2025-11-04 before treating the mismatch as closed.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The airway bill links SHP-000411 to IE-2025-000411 but provides no `supplier_id`; the packet manifest lists six files and no shipment-specific supplier declaration."
"The reference lookup says no current document was found for SUP-02/P1006 and expressly says absence from the register does not prove that no document exists outside it."
"The only Irish-origin register entry supplied for P1006 is SUP-02, valid 2025-01-01 to 2025-07-31 and marked ‘Expired in register’; the shipment date is 2025-09-18."

dimensions.name: Reasoning and hypothesis testing
citations: "‘Preference=Yes proves the claim’: rejected because the indicator is a declaration field in `declaration.pdf`, while the packet lacks a linked supplier declaration"
"‘US ERP origin proves the claim is false’: rejected because `origin-workshop.md` explicitly says Helios is not a preference-proof system"
"‘The expired SUP-02 entry is sufficient’: rejected by its 2025-07-31 end date versus the 2025-09-18 entry date."

dimensions.name: Calibration
citations: "The evidence supports ‘unsupported on this packet,’ not ‘false’ or ‘fraud.’"
"Unsupported is not the same as false. Verdict: unsupported, not disproved."
"Failure to find a linked record does not prove the claim false because the reference and workshop warn that evidence may exist outside the register."

dimensions.name: Process and system understanding
citations: "the workshop says manufacturing origin was never designed to prove preference."
"Resolving which supplier fulfilled this shipment and obtaining their valid declaration from `supplier_origin_register.csv` or procurement folders per `origin-workshop.md` is the required proof."
"the packet does not identify which supplier sourced this shipment."

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Hold the preference claim pending supplier-specific proof, request the declaration and governing rule from Procurement/Customs, and do not clear it as preferential until verified."
"this hold is reversible and no duty change should be assumed until tariff treatment is confirmed."
"Distinguishing unverified documentation from intentional misdeclaration ensures that administrative holds precede any formal compliance escalation."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "A current document would be required" is directionally reasonable, but the applicable preferential rule and its validity requirements are not actually supplied or quoted; the conclusion should remain conditional on that rule.

"SUP-03/05/06 plus valid proof could support preference; SUP-01/US would support non-preferential treatment" is appropriately conditional, but supplier register origin alone may not establish that the supplier fulfilled this shipment or that the product met the applicable qualifying rule.
The submission treats 2025-09-18 as the shipment date while citing the declaration date; it should explicitly establish that these dates are the relevant shipment and preference dates.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The preference claim may be valid because the shipment could have been sourced from SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06, or supported by a qualifying supplier declaration stored outside the incomplete register; alternatively, the declaration may contain an administrative preference error. The packet alone does not distinguish these possibilities.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Quote the exact supplier, shipment-date, and applicable-rule fields from the purchase or logistics records, then obtain and assess the supplier-specific declaration against the governing preferential-origin rule before deciding whether to clear or correct the claim.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "185 of 262 `qcore_release_ts` values are exactly 02:10:00"; cites `batch_release.csv` and `source_freshness.csv` with field-level specificity.
"The SOP defines the routine target from required evidence being available to disposition"; cites `qc_release_sop.md` and the `batch_release.csv` header.
"The 42 HOLD rows are open/right-censored"; cites disposition and receipt/release fields, while acknowledging completed-only bias.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "Headline cycle time of 1.5 days conflates physical receipt-to-release ... with the SOP-mandated evidence-to-release standard" separates the reported symptom from the governing metric.

"the observed 02:10:00 timestamp clustering represents a batch-processing synchronization artifact rather than actual release timing" identifies a plausible mechanism and connects it to source freshness.
The submission tests alternatives including genuine process speed, data corruption, and stale COA status, but treats the default-timestamp mechanism as more established than the evidence proves.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "the extract has no timestamp for certificate/specification/deviation evidence availability" clearly identifies a decision-relevant missing field.
The evidence table uses confidence labels and calls COA lag versus real control gaps "Medium-High" uncertainty.

"represents a ... synchronization artifact" is stated too definitively; matching an extract timestamp to a snapshot time does not by itself prove the timestamp is a default rather than an interface commit or actual event time.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Decision: Defer KPI dashboard publication pending timestamp verification" appropriately reframes the task around metric validity rather than optimizing an invalid KPI.
"Do one read-only validation of 5–10 02:10-stamped batches ... before building a dashboard" is small, reversible, and operationally safe.
The recommendation protects against publishing a misleading management metric while preserving a path to a scoped KPI if validation succeeds.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: The submission explicitly rejects "The 1.5-day headline reflects genuine process speed" and "Discard the extract as corrupt."
It proposes live QCore audit to distinguish authentic timestamps from extract artifacts and reconciliation to distinguish stale COA status from real control gaps.
The strongest competing explanation—that 02:10 is an interface commit or genuine release time despite snapshot concentration—is not fully separated from the claimed defaulting mechanism.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Live QCore audit for a sample of the 185 stamped rows" directly tests the timestamp-semantics question.
"`evidence_available_ts` or a validated field mapping for 5–10 batches" targets the minimum evidence needed to calculate the SOP clock.
The submission explains how each result would change the launch decision and also requests targeted follow-up for right-censoring and COA freshness.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 185 timestamps are "defaulted to 02:10:00" is stronger than the supplied evidence supports; concentration at the snapshot time establishes an anomaly, not whether the values are defaults, interface commits, or actual event times.

The phrase "excluding those completed rows gives an evidence-to-release median of about 8.4 hours" is potentially misleading because `evidence_available_ts` is explicitly missing; this appears to be a proxy calculation, not a measured evidence-to-release median.
The assertion that the 42 HOLD rows are "likely to become the slowest observations" is plausible but not demonstrated by the extract and should remain a hypothesis.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 values may be legitimate QCore interface-commit timestamps or actual release times rather than defaulted values. In that case, the extract could still support a release-to-interface KPI, but not necessarily the SOP evidence-availability KPI; an event or decision timestamp is needed to distinguish those interpretations.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Rename the 8.4-hour result explicitly as a proxy, remove the assertion that timestamps are definitively defaulted, and prioritize a read-only comparison of QCore audit/event timestamps with the extract for a small sample, including the field definition and source snapshot times.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "Revision-B valve supply is two free units... against four units of revision-B demand" — cites specific files, request IDs, revision, and quantity evidence; the cross-file chain is strong, though underlying row-level details are summarized rather than shown.

"The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June while the request export is associated with the 24 July ProcureNet snapshot" — explicitly identifies source freshness and counterevidence to immediate availability.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "A semantic-search hit means transfer it: rejected" — tests identity/search against reservation and stock constraints rather than treating similarity as equivalence.
"Same part family means interchangeable: rejected" — distinguishes revision and site-specific qualification from description similarity.
"An expensive semantic-search system is required: rejected" — uses the exact-MPN result as evidence, but the conclusion remains partly untested for the 11 blank-MPN requests.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers" — appropriately limits the decision.
"Actionable now still requires current confirmation" — recognizes that stale global stock prevents full certainty.

"Needs check" and "Not transferable" classifications, plus conditional language such as "moves candidates toward actionable," provide claim-specific uncertainty, although calling the eight-request slice actionable now is somewhat stronger than the stale-data evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value" — separates candidate/gross value from a more defensible actionable subset.
"Do not convert raw search hits into automatic transfers" — protects against operational and engineering risk.
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search on 24 requests" — proposes a small, reversible test that can determine whether a semantic-search investment is justified.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "The hypothesis survives only if those records are wrong, requiring a live CMMS check" — preserves a plausible alternative rather than treating the reservation data as infallible.
"Only documented engineering approval could reverse this rejection" — states what evidence could revive the revision-substitution hypothesis.
The submission actively tests three plausible failure modes, but does not yet test whether semantic search adds valid recall for the blank-MPN population.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: "Manufacturer part number and revision from local maintenance records" — requests targeted identity evidence for the 11 blank-MPN requests.
"Live local CMMS reservation and availability query" — directly addresses the stale/negative availability issue.
"Receiving engineer and qualification approval" — identifies the decision owner and evidence needed for substitutions and site-specific parts.
"Compare recall/precision of exact MPN join versus semantic search on 24 requests" — specifies a discriminating evaluation and its decision impact.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "The brief assumes search recall is the constraint, but semantic search is not the real problem" is premature: no semantic-search recall or precision test has been reported for the 11 blank-MPN requests.

"An exact MPN join resolves all 13 identified requests immediately" overstates the result because the join retrieves candidates, while freshness, reservation, revision, UOM, qualification, and allocation still determine transferability.
The eight requests labeled "Actionable now" remain conditional on live confirmation, so "actionable now" should preferably be phrased as provisionally actionable or ready for confirmation.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Exact-MPN matching may solve only the identified subset; semantic search could still provide material value for the 11 blank-MPN requests if it generates valid candidates that can then pass engineering, revision, qualification, reservation, and current-availability checks. The available evidence supports semantic search as a candidate-generation pilot, not yet dismissal as unnecessary.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run the proposed blinded comparison on the 11 blank-MPN requests: obtain authoritative MPN/revision labels from local maintenance records, compare exact-join and semantic-search candidate recall and precision, then validate candidates against a current CMMS availability/reservation extract. This would directly test the central claim that data cleanup, rather than semantic retrieval, is the binding constraint.
